Collaborating with a vibrant, inclusive, global team? It’s all possible with a role at Videojet, a Veralto company. You have likely purchased or used a product touched by Videojet Technologies this week—after all, Videojet is a world leader in the product identification market, providing in-line printing, coding and marking products, consumables, and software solutions. Videojet’s technologies play a critical role in ensuring the safety and authenticity of products sold across the globe in the food, beverage, pharmaceutical, and industrial marketplaces. As part of the Videojet team and the broader Veralto network, you’ll work with products that make an everyday impact on the world around you—and along the way, you’ll have opportunities to make your mark on our business and your career, deepen your skillset, and pursue your ambitions. Learn about our leading portfolio of innovative products here: https://cdn.videojet.com/U309KOI6/as/vvpm76xpvfqj3kgchf7khbnz/vf-history-of-videojet-innovation-us We Offer A remote role supporting a highly visible global technology program. Professional onboarding and training. Career development opportunities across Videojet and Veralto. The opportunity to work with an inclusive, international team. Reporting to the Director, Service & Commercial Applications, the Global Communications Systems Engineer will support the European rollout and ongoing development of Videojet’s customer-facing communications technology. You will help deploy, integrate, and improve the NICE CXone contact center platform and its CRM connections while partnering with service, commercial, integration, and global DTS teams. This remote role may be based in any EMEA location and requires availability during European business hours. This role has no routine travel requirement. Occasional travel may be requested for selected larger-country rollouts, depending on business needs. In this role, a typical day will look like: Coordinate with local service and commercial teams, integration teams, and global development partners to deliver contact center rollouts and dependable post-launch support across Europe. Translate business requirements into technical specifications, balancing platform constraints, user experience, cost, and business value. Develop, configure, and enhance NICE CXone features, call flows, logic-based business rules, alerts, process flows, integrations, and automation. Provide hands-on support for telephony and communication applications, troubleshoot technical issues, and identify opportunities to improve reliability and the customer experience. Create SOPs, standard work, onboarding materials, and training for users and managers within local business organizations. Build and maintain reports, dashboards, data-quality controls, and KPIs that improve productivity, adoption, and continuous improvement. The essential requirements of the job include: Hands-on experience developing, deploying, configuring, or supporting contact center platforms or software. Working knowledge of telephony technologies, including PSTN/POTS and VoIP/SIP. Experience integrating a contact center platform with Salesforce or another CRM system. Experience gathering business requirements, producing functional or technical designs, and developing and executing tests. A degree or certification in IT, telecommunications, programming, or a related technical field, or equivalent directly relevant practical experience, together with advanced to fluent written and spoken English for technical and business communication. It would be a plus if you also possess: Experience with NICE CXone and Salesforce. Programming or application-development experience. Experience supporting multi-country technology rollouts. Experience developing user training, reports, or dashboards. Proficiency in another major European language. Videojet is proud to be part of the Product Quality & Innovation segment of Veralto (NYSE: VLTO), a global leader dedicated to ensuring access to clean water, safe food and medicine, and trusted essential goods. When you join Veralto’s vibrant global network of associates, you join a unique culture and work environment where purpose meets possibility: where the work you do has an everyday impact on the resources and essentials we all rely on, and where you’ll have valuable opportunities to deepen your skillset, pursue your ambitions, and grow your career. Together, we’re Safeguarding the World’s Most Vital Resources™—and building rewarding careers along the way. At Veralto, we value diversity and the existence of similarities and differences, both visible and not, found in our workforce, workplace and throughout the markets we serve. Our associates, customers and shareholders contribute unique and different perspectives as a result of these diverse attributes. The Advanced Staff Thermal Systems Engineer fosters innovation and consistency by developing and being accountable for system-level architectures and execution. In cooperation with the Program Management team, the Aerospace Thermal Systems Engineer leads technical development projects. During the program, the Advanced Staff Thermal Systems Engineer manages a multi-disciplinary project team of subject matter experts in fields such as thermal analysis, installation, mechanical design and analysis, reliability, controls, electronics and software, and testing. Additionally, as a member of the senior technical staff the Advanced Staff Thermal Systems Engineer serves as a technical leader within the Intergalactic engineering group. This individual collaborates with company and other technical leaders, leads and mentors junior staff, and participates in development of the technical team. Job Description Roles and Responsibilities : Develop and be responsible for program’s architecture and technical approach. This can include thermal and controls analysis, reliability analysis, solid modeling, testing, stress analysis, and other accepted methods in aerospace. Serve as technical lead for programs, provide clear objectives that are measurable and attainable, and coordinate technical activities with internal resources (engineers across different functional groups) and external resources (vendors, contractors). Identify and manage program’s technical risks and work closely with the Program Manager to ensure successful execution of development programs. Manage and account for technical requirements from the top down – traceability, decomposition, derivation, and verification & validation. Allocate and decompose high-level requirements into lower-level specifications to internal functional groups, components, and suppliers as applicable. Serve as technical leader in the company contributing to technical strategy and growth/maturation of the engineering team and community. Research and recommend investments or changes in technology, toolsets, procedures, equipment, systems, etc. to continually improve Intergalactic’ s products and services. Communicate and collaborate with customers and suppliers as part of design development process. Review and approve documentation for transition from prototype to production. Provide engineering support to trouble shoot and diagnose non-performing products (RCCA, lessons learned, etc.). Required Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university and a Minimum of 5 years’ experience in Systems Engineering, preferably within Thermal Management Systems. Desired Characteristics & Experience Bachelor’s degree in engineering from an accredited university or college, with 15+ years of work experience in Systems Engineering, preferably within Thermal Management Systems Working knowledge of key aerospace technical disciplines including requirements management, technical verification and validation methodologies, mechanical design, materials, modeling/documentation, structural analysis, thermal fluid sciences, electrical systems, system controls, embedded controls, development testing and analysis, qualification analysis and testing. Excellent interpersonal relationship building both internally and externally. Understanding of aerospace requirements management methodologies and processes – traceability, decomposition, derivation verification, and validation. Functional understanding of major aircraft systems: environmental control systems, powerplant, electrical, hydraulics, controls, avionics, power generation, and structures. Experience with Vapor Cycle Systems (VCS), Liquid Cooling Systems (LCS) and/or Air Cycle Systems (ACS) Experience and working knowledge of standard components in VCS, LCS, and ACS such as heat exchangers, pumps, compressors, turbines, fans, valves, motor and motor controllers, water collectors/separators, etc. Familiarity with environmental testing and qualification methods such as MIL-STD-810 and DO-160 Experience with requirements management tools, and model-based systems engineering (MBSE) tools and processes heavily desired Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal and leadership skills. Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems. Demonstrated ability to lead programs / projects. Ability to document, plan, market, and execute programs. Established project management skills. review_candidates.title: Nutanix Migration Engineer
review_candidates.description: Details: Job Description The Nutanix Migration Engineer is the technical executor of the VMware-to-Nutanix transition. The role spans the full migration lifecycle - assessment and sizing, migration design, Nutanix Move 6.0 execution, cutover, validation, troubleshooting, and post-migration stabilization. This is a delivery-focused engineering role: the expectation is independent, hands-on execution inside a production healthcare environment where failed cutovers and extended outages are not recoverable events. The engineer must be equally comfortable on the VMware source side and the Nutanix target side, because the majority of migration failures originate in the source estate rather than the destination. Job Requirements Details: Perform discovery of the source VMware estate using Nutanix Collector, RVTools, and native vCenter reporting - capturing VM inventory, resource consumption, disk layout, snapshots, VMware Tools state, guest OS versions, and network configuration. Analyze workload characteristics to identify migration blockers before scheduling: unsupported guest operating systems, RDMs, shared VMDKs, oversized disks, encrypted VMs, VMs with attached ISOs, static IP dependencies, application clustering, and licensing anchored to hardware identifiers. Support target sizing and capacity planning using Nutanix Sizer - validating CPU, memory, storage, and node count against actual measured consumption rather than allocated values. Group workloads into migration waves by application dependency, business criticality, downtime tolerance, and owner availability; document per-wave migration approach and rollback plan. Produce the migration design and cutover runbook for each wave: pre-checks, sequence, validation steps, back-out procedure, and named approvers. Deploy, configure, and maintain Nutanix Move 6.0 - appliance sizing, source and target environment registration, credential and permission configuration, and network mapping between source port groups and AHV virtual networks. Build and execute migration plans: seed data replication, monitor replication progress and lag, manage bandwidth and concurrency limits, and coordinate cutover timing with application owners. Manage guest preparation - VirtIO driver injection for Windows guests, Linux guest readiness, VMware Tools removal, and IP retention or reassignment per the network design. Execute cutovers within approved change windows, including final delta sync, source VM shutdown, target power-on, and confirmation of guest boot, network reachability, and service startup. Handle migration exceptions where Move is not the right tool - in-guest methods, backup-and-restore migration via the client's backup platform, database-native replication, or rebuild-and-reinstall for legacy or unsupported workloads. Execute post-migration validation: guest OS health, VirtIO device and driver state, disk presence and capacity, network and DNS resolution, application service startup, backup job re-registration, and monitoring agent check-in. Troubleshoot migration failures across the stack - Move appliance and agent errors, CBT and snapshot issues, vCenter permission and API failures, source datastore performance limits, boot failures on AHV (UEFI/BIOS mismatch, missing drivers, disk controller changes), and post-cutover network isolation. Coordinate application owner validation and formal acceptance sign-off for each migrated workload; drive open defects to closure within the agreed hypercare window. Perform post-migration optimization: right-sizing CPU and memory, storage container and compression/dedupe policy alignment, VM affinity rules, and protection policy or replication configuration on the target. Decommission source objects only after acceptance and retention criteria are met, following the agreed decommissioning checklist. Maintain as-built documentation, migration logs, exception records, and lessons learned; contribute reusable runbook content back to the Stefanini Nutanix practice. 5+ years in enterprise virtualization or infrastructure engineering, including 2+ years hands-on with Nutanix in production. Demonstrable participation in at least one completed enterprise VMware-to-Nutanix migration - candidates must be able to describe scale, tooling, failure modes encountered, and how they were resolved. Required certification: Nutanix Certified Professional - Multicloud Infrastructure (NCP-MCI), current version. Preferred: Nutanix Certified Master - Multicloud Infrastructure (NCM-MCI), VMware Certified Professional - Data Center Virtualization (VCP-DCV), Microsoft or Red Hat OS-level certification. Experience in a healthcare or other regulated production environment, working within formal change control and maintenance windows.
